question: The United Nations adopted the 'Charter of Economic Rights and Duties of States' in ______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sun Dec 01 1974 00:00:00 GMT+0530 (India Standard Time)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The 'Charter of Economic Rights and Duties of States' was adopted by the United Nations General Assembly on 12 December 1974.
 
• This charter outlines the economic rights and duties of states and emphasizes the principles of sovereign equality, non-interference, and mutual benefit among nations.
 
• The charter was adopted through the resolution 3281 (XXIX) of the United Nations General Assembly.
 
• It reflects the collective efforts and aspirations of the developing countries to establish a new international economic order.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **United Nations General Assembly (UNGA)**

 
 
• The UNGA is one of the six principal organs of the United Nations, serving as its main deliberative, policymaking, and representative organ.
 
• It is composed of all 193 member states of the UN, each with one vote.
 
• The General Assembly meets once a year in a regular session, but special and emergency sessions can also be convened.
 
 
 
• **New International Economic Order (NIEO)**
 
 
• The NIEO was a set of proposals put forward during the 1970s by developing countries through the United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD) to promote their interests by improving their terms of trade, increasing development assistance, developed-country tariff reductions, and other means.
 
• The NIEO aimed to address the economic disparities between the developed and developing countries.
 
 
 
• **Resolution 3281 (XXIX)**
 
 
• This resolution, also known as the 'Charter of Economic Rights and Duties of States', was adopted by the General Assembly on 12 December 1974.
 
• It consists of various articles outlining the economic rights and duties of states, focusing on sovereignty over natural resources, economic cooperation, and the right to development.
